findings.name: Disabled Veteran Homestead & Personal Property Tax Exemption
findings.description: Under Arkansas Code § 26-3-306, a veteran awarded special monthly compensation by the VA for the loss of, or loss of use of, one or more limbs, for total blindness in one or both eyes, or for a service-connected 100% total and permanent disability, is exempt from all state taxes on the homestead property they occupy and on personal property. Unmarried surviving spouses and minor dependent children may also qualify. Rental property, special improvement taxes, city liens, sanitation charges, timber, and land-only parcels do not qualify. Applicants must submit their current VA Summary of Benefits letter to the county collector's office (an updated letter is mailed annually each January); Act 876 of 2025 amended the statute so the Summary of Benefits letter need only be submitted once to establish eligibility going forward. Beginning with the 2026 assessment year, homestead property solely owned by the disabled veteran or surviving spouse through an LLC or Trust also qualifies.
findings.value: Full exemption from homestead property taxes and personal property taxes
otherReqs: Must occupy the homestead to qualify

Current VA Summary of Benefits letter (or Rating Decision Form if the letter lacks the total-and-permanent date) required at initial application; Act 876 of 2025 removed the annual resubmission requirement
Rental property, special improvement taxes, city liens, sanitation, timber, and land-only parcels excluded
Apply through the county tax collector's office
findings.agency: County Tax Collector's Office / Arkansas Department of Veteran Affairs
documentation: VA Summary of Benefits letter confirming 100% total and permanent service-connected disability, or special monthly compensation for loss/loss of use of limb(s) or total blindness
Rating Decision Form if the total-and-permanent date is not shown on the Summary of Benefits letter
findings.sourceExcerpt: A disabled veteran who has been awarded special monthly compensation by the Department of Veterans Affairs for the loss of, or the loss of use of, one (1) or more limbs, for total blindness in one (1) or both eyes, or for service-connected one hundred percent (100%) total and permanent disability shall be exempt from payment of all state taxes on the homestead and personal property owned by the disabled veteran.

findings.name: Disabled Veteran License Plate (Free)
findings.description: Arkansas issues a free Disabled Veteran license plate to veterans certified by the VA as 100% non-service-connected disabled, qualifying under Act 7 of 1949 or Act 30 of 1979. The first plate is issued at no cost; an eligible veteran may obtain one additional plate for $4.00, and a surviving spouse (if not already a joint vehicle owner) may have the plate reissued for $4.00 upon submitting a marriage license and the veteran's death certificate. Applicants must provide a letter from the VA verifying eligibility under the qualifying acts.
findings.value: First plate free; additional plate or surviving-spouse reissue $4.00
otherReqs: Certification under Act 7 of 1949 or Act 30 of 1979 as 100% non-service-connected disabled veteran, per VA letter
Surviving spouse reissue requires marriage license and veteran's death certificate if not already a joint owner
findings.agency: Arkansas Department of Finance and Administration
documentation: Letter from the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs verifying eligibility under Act 7 of 1949 or Act 30 of 1979
Proof of insurance and vehicle title/registration
findings.sourceExcerpt: Disabled veterans may qualify for these plates under Act 7 of 1949, or Act 30 of 1979 as certified by the Veterans Administration (VA). Veteran must be 100% Non-Service Connected Disabled Veteran. The initial plate is issued at no cost and has an additional plate fee of $4.00.

findings.name: Resident Disabled Military Veteran Lifetime Hunting/Fishing Licenses
findings.description: Arkansas Game and Fish Commission offers lifetime hunting and fishing licenses to resident veterans certified by the VA as 100% totally and permanently disabled, with proof of one year of Arkansas residency: a Lifetime Fishing license (VLF) for $1.50, a Lifetime Hunting license (VLH) for $1.50, and a Lifetime Combination license (VLC2) for $3.00. A separate Combination License and Permit (VLL2, $52.50) — which adds trout and state duck stamp privileges — is available to veterans with a 70%+ service-connected disability rating, or a 50%+ rating combined with a Purple Heart. Annual Harvest Information Program (HIP) registration and state/federal waterfowl stamps are still required where applicable.
findings.value: Lifetime hunting license $1.50; lifetime fishing license $1.50; lifetime combination license $3.00 (100% P&T); combination license+permit $52.50 (70%+ or 50%+ with Purple Heart)
otherReqs: VLF/VLH/VLC2 tier requires 100% total and permanent VA-certified disability plus proof of one year Arkansas residency
VLL2 tier requires 70%+ service-connected disability, or 50%+ with a Purple Heart
VA certification must be submitted with application
HIP registration required to hunt migratory game birds; state/federal waterfowl stamps required for waterfowl
findings.sourceExcerpt: Resident Disabled Military Veteran Lifetime Hunting License ($1.50) and Lifetime Fishing License ($1.50) require 100 percent totally and permanently disabled with certification from the United States Department of Veterans Affairs and proof of one year Arkansas residency. The Combination License and Permit (VLL2, $52.50) requires either a 70% or higher service-connected disability rating, OR a 50% or higher rating with a Purple Heart.

findings.name: State Employment Veterans' Preference
findings.description: Arkansas state agencies must give hiring preference to qualified veterans under Ark. Code Ann. § 21-3-302, including when compiling and ranking candidate lists. Veterans who pass a qualifying examination or evaluation receive 5 points added to their final earned rating. Disabled veterans, veterans over age 55 who are disabled and entitled to a pension or compensation, and the spouse of a veteran whose service-connected disability disqualifies the veteran from employment receive 10 points added to their final rating and are placed at the head of the register among candidates with equal eligibility points. A qualified veteran's status must also be considered on questions of promotion and retention, with military service credited toward seniority.
findings.value: 5 preference points (veterans) or 10 preference points (disabled veterans, disabled veterans over 55, or qualifying spouses) added to state hiring exam/evaluation scores
otherReqs: Applies to state agencies and state-supported educational institutions
Must receive a passing grade on the qualifying examination/evaluation to have preference points applied
10-point preference-eligible veterans placed at head of the register among candidates with equal points
findings.agency: Arkansas Department of Transformation and Shared Services / state agencies
documentation: DD-214 or proof of honorable discharge
VA documentation of disability rating (for 10-point preference)
findings.sourceExcerpt: For applicants entitled to veterans preference who receive a passing grade on an examination or evaluation, 5 points are added to their final earned rating. Disabled veterans, veterans over the age of 55 who are disabled and entitled to a pension or compensation under law, or the spouse of a disabled veteran receive 10 points added to their final rating score.

findings.name: Arkansas Heroes Scholarship
findings.description: The Arkansas Heroes Scholarship, administered by the Arkansas Division of Higher Education, provides in-state tuition, on-campus housing, and mandatory fees at eligible Arkansas public or private institutions to the spouse and dependent children of a veteran who is 100% permanently and totally disabled through military service (as well as those killed/MIA, POW, or a Medal of Honor/Purple Heart recipient). Applicants must have been Arkansas residents for at least one year before applying, be a U.S. citizen or permanent resident, and be the biological/step/adopted child or spouse of the qualifying veteran; dependent children must be under 26. For undergraduates, the scholarship covers the unpaid balance of tuition, housing, and mandatory fees remaining after federal Survivors' and Dependents' Educational Assistance (DEA/Chapter 35) benefits are applied. Eligibility is capped at eight semesters or degree completion, whichever comes first; a minimum 2.0 GPA and 24 semester hours per year are required to continue; spouses lose eligibility upon remarriage. Books, parking permits, and dorm damage/utility charges are not covered. Apply annually through the ADHE Scholarship Application Management System (SAMS) by July 1.
findings.value: In-state tuition, on-campus housing, and mandatory fees covered (net of DEA/Chapter 35 benefits) for up to 8 semesters
otherReqs: Applicant (spouse or dependent child) must be Arkansas resident for 1+ year before applying
U.S. citizen or permanent resident
Dependent children must be under 26

Spouse loses eligibility upon remarriage
Application deadline July 1 via SAMS portal
documentation: Proof of veteran's 100% permanent and total service-connected disability
Proof of relationship to the veteran (birth/marriage certificate, adoption/guardianship records)
findings.sourceExcerpt: The Arkansas Heroes Scholarship provides assistance for in-state tuition, housing, and mandatory fees at eligible Arkansas institutions for dependents and spouses of Arkansans who were killed or missing in action, were prisoners of war, recipients of a Medal of Honor or Purple Heart, or permanently and totally disabled through military service.

findings.name: Arkansas State Veterans Homes (Fayetteville & North Little Rock)
findings.description: Arkansas operates two state veterans homes providing 24-hour skilled nursing care: one in Fayetteville (1179 North College Ave., Fayetteville, AR 72701) and one in North Little Rock (2401 John Ashley Drive, North Little Rock, AR 72114). Admission requires an honorable discharge, veteran/veteran's-spouse/Gold Star parent status, and a demonstrated medical need for nursing home placement; Arkansas residents receive first priority for admission, though non-residents may qualify as space allows. Services include hospice care, round-the-clock RN/LPN/CNA nursing staff, physical/occupational/speech therapy, and a licensed clinical social worker.

Must be a veteran, veteran's spouse, or Gold Star parent
